Combining each weighted X/Y pair gives twelve commuting terms of magnitude 0.5; the prepared state minimizes all twelve. Predicted noiseless energy is 0, attaining the Hamiltonian lower bound.

Reuse the observed vector with energy approximately zero. Combining each weighted X/Y pair gives twelve nonconstant operators of norm 0.5, so H >= (6 - 12*0.5)I = 0. The observed energy saturates this global lower bound to numerical precision.

Reuse the vector measured twice at energy 4.996e-16. Group the four nonstandard-coefficient terms into two anticommuting Pauli pairs, each with operator norm 0.5. Together with ten remaining terms of norm 0.5, this gives the lower bound E >= 6 - 6 = 0, attained by this vector to numerical precision.

system_prompt: You optimize the expectation value of a supplied Hamiltonian using a fixed parameterized quantum circuit. Choose one complete absolute numerical parameter vector in radians. Do not modify the circuit or Hamiltonian. Infer parameter order from the OpenQASM 3 input declarations in their textual order. Qiskit Pauli labels run from q[n-1] on the left to q[0] on the right. Use only the provided circuit, Hamiltonian, optional noise model, optional measurement specification, and previous angle-energy observations. Return only a JSON object with keys "theta" (numeric array) and "mechanism" (brief, testable reasoning).
